patients.summary: Healthy young swim instructor with mild intermittent atopic dermatitis who joins the practice in 2022. In 2025 she has a left swimmer's ear treated by ENT and a first anaphylaxis to shrimp; a second shrimp anaphylaxis in February 2026 precedes her allergy consult.

events.reason: New patient, establish care and physical

medications.sig: Apply a thin layer to affected areas twice daily as needed for eczema flare
Apply liberally to dry skin daily for maintenance

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT / PREVENTIVE

23 y/o woman joining the practice. Previously seen at another primary care office; records request signed today.

Concerns: none acute. Has had eczema since she was little, mostly backs of knees, inner elbows and hands. Flares a few times a year, usually winter. Uses triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID for a few days when it flares and plain petroleum jelly daily the rest of the time. Wants refills to be possible through us.

PMH: atopic dermatitis, mild/intermittent.
PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID prn flare; petroleum jelly daily.
Allergies: no drug allergies. Dust mites and seasonal pollen.
FHx: mother asthma and allergic rhinitis. Father eczema. Maternal uncle allergic to shellfish.
Social: swim instructor, teaches lessons at an indoor pool most weekdays plus Saturday mornings. Never smoked. 1-2 drinks a week. Single, lives in Northampton. Exercises in the pool, obviously.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap 2021 per pt, normal. Sexually active, condoms. Agrees to GC/CT screen.

ROS: negative except skin as above.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, BMI about 22. Well appearing. HEENT: canals clear, TMs normal. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid normal. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT. Skin: a little dryness of the dorsal hands and both antecubital fossae, no active plaques, no excoriation. Neuro grossly normal.

PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. Atopic dermatitis, mild intermittent: well controlled. Continue emollient daily and triamcinolone for short flare courses. Discussed rinsing off and moisturizing right after the pool.
2. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, one-time HIV and hep C screen, GC/CT urine. Tdap today (last one she thinks was middle school; will confirm with old records). Flu and COVID booster at a nurse visit next month. Pap due 2024 if 2021 result confirmed.
3. Return yearly for physical, sooner prn. She knows she can text/call.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Tdap 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Screening questions answered no. VIS given. Tolerated without issue.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Taylor, everything from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV, hepatitis C, gonorrhea and chlamydia screens were all negative. Nothing to follow up on. See you for your flu shot next month.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records from prior primary care office received by secure fax, 22 pages, scanned to chart.

Abstracted by PCP:
- Problem: eczema since childhood, topical steroid as needed.
- Immunizations: childhood series complete; HPV series complete; Tdap 2011.
- Pap 2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Wisdom teeth extracted 2018, oral surgeon, uneventful.
- No hospitalizations. No drug allergies.
Next Pap due 2024.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after work for vaccines. No fever or illness today, no prior vaccine reactions. Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Pfizer bivalent COVID booster 0.3 mL IM L deltoid. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Next due fall 2023.

documents.title: Eczema cream
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! My hands are doing the winter thing again, cracking around the knuckles. I'm almost out of the triamcinolone, can you send a new tube to my pharmacy? Thanks

documents.title: RE: Eczema cream
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent - 80 g tube with a refill. Twice a day on the cracked spots for up to two weeks, then back to just the petroleum jelly. Gloves for dishes help, and a thick layer at night under cotton gloves if it's bad. If it isn't settling in two weeks or looks infected (weeping, yellow crust) send me a picture.

documents.title: Missed Appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 8:30 physical. Called, she apologized, had a lesson schedule change and forgot. Rebooked 10/17 at 8:00.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL

Doing well. Busy fall teaching season. Skin: one flare last February on the hands, cleared with the cream; otherwise just moisturizer. No other concerns.

Meds: triamcinolone 0.1% cream prn, petroleum jelly daily.
Allergies: NKDA; dust mites, seasonal pollen.
Social unchanged: never smoker, a drink or two a week. Condoms.

ROS negative.

Exam: vitals reviewed, weight stable. Well. HEENT normal, canals clear. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Skin mildly dry on hands, no active eczema.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Atopic dermatitis, quiet. Continue routine.
- GC/CT urine today (under 25).
- Flu + updated COVID today.
- Pap next year.
- RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your urine screen from Tuesday was negative. All set until next fall.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Eczema flare x3 weeks, both hands and inner elbows, itchy, worse at night. Been in the pool more than usual covering for another instructor. Used the triamcinolone a few days and stopped when it looked better, then it came right back. No oozing, no fever.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Dorsal hands with ill-defined erythematous, dry, lichenified patches with a few excoriations; similar patches both antecubital fossae. No crusting, no vesicles, no signs of infection.

A: Atopic dermatitis flare, mild, partially treated.

P: Use the triamcinolone 0.1% BID for a full 2 weeks this time, then twice weekly on the usual spots for a month. Shower right after the pool and put the petroleum jelly on within a few minutes while skin is damp. Fragrance-free soap. Refill sent. Return if not clearly better in 3 weeks.

documents.title: Prescription Sent
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: triamcinolone acetonide 0.1% cream, 80 g, 1 refill. Apply to affected areas twice daily for 2 weeks, then twice weekly to usual areas. E-prescribed to patient's pharmacy.

reports.text:
Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation.
Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present.
Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM).

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, turned 25 last month.

Interval: February eczema flare on the hands settled after the full 2-week course; using the cream once in a while since. No ER or urgent care visits. Feels well.

Meds: triamcinolone 0.1% cream prn; petroleum jelly.
Allergies: NKDA; dust mites; seasonal pollen.
Social: still teaching swim, never smoker, 1-2 drinks/wk.
GYN: regular cycles, condoms. Last Pap 2021 normal.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. General well. HEENT: canals clear, TMs pearly. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vaginal mucosa normal, cervix without lesions; Pap collected. Skin: faint dryness dorsal hands only.

PHQ-9: 1.

A/P
- Health maintenance: Pap (cytology) sent. GC/CT urine. Flu and updated COVID today.
- Atopic dermatitis: quiet, continue.
- See next fall.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Taylor - your Pap came back normal and the urine screen was negative. Next Pap would be in 3 years, fall 2027.
